title: The Voynich manuscript: Symbol roles revisited
authors: Vladimír Matlach, Barbora Anna Janečková and Daniel Dostál
summary: The authors measure autocorrelation of successive intervals between occurrences of the same EVA symbol. They separately propose a heuristic for possible ligatures and discuss a hypothetical numeric encoding.
established: In the processed Takahashi transcript, the authors report positive and individually significant estimates for 90.1% of 760 lag-by-symbol tests over lags 1 to 40. The reported confidence limits are pointwise.
A Timm–Schinner generated sample comes closest to the manuscript by mean autocorrelation among the compared texts. The manuscript remains the maximum in that comparison.

The ligature loss weights were adjusted on Latin and Arabic examples, then fixed for an Armenian example and planted English and Czech examples. Each designated held-apart triplet ranked inside the authors' fifth-percentile criterion. The manuscript candidates remain hypotheses and in some cases the authors manually inspect discrepant occurrences.

open.question: How much of the long-lag symbol-gap autocorrelation survives after controlling for local rates and the line layout?
open.check: Use paired public ZL and Takahashi samples. Freeze symbol preprocessing and measure Pearson gap autocorrelations over lags 1 to 40. Compare a global token-word shuffle with matched within-page line and paragraph-word shuffles, and with pinned self-citation and fitted stationary whole-copy controls on the same public layout. Report coefficients and an aggregate lag statistic against each null before interpreting pointwise significance. Estimate sensitivity with known rate changes and with known dependence at constant rates.

open.question: Can the published glyph-triplet score distinguish proposed ligatures from ordinary compound-like distributions in matched controls?
open.check: Fix the published loss weights and candidate threshold. Evaluate all triplets both in public natural text with and without independent planted ligatures and in a stationary line-chain control. Record false-positive ranks, then check fixed manuscript candidates across ZL and Takahashi and use a separate public scan sample to evaluate disputed occurrences.
